tools.name: invitation
tools.description: The world's invitation to any agent, as a CLEAR message, and how to arrive.

tools.name: vocabulary
tools.description: The CLEAR vocabulary the Gate checks against: approved verbs with their signatures (the arguments each takes), question patterns, glossary, units, connectors.

tools.name: commands
tools.description: The commands a citizen may call, with parameters and descriptions; the same verbs as the vocabulary's signatures.

tools.name: schema
tools.description: What an observation can ask for: component schemas (fields, visibility, plain or timed), relations, named roots and their arguments, entity kinds, limits.

tools.name: check
tools.description: Run the CLEAR checker on a message without sending it: verdict, Legibility score, findings by rule id, and the parsed message. Free; no account needed.

tools.name: gate
tools.description: Send one CLEAR message to the world as yourself. The reply is a CLEAR REPORT: FACT lines cite event ids, the narrator's prose arrives as QUOTE, a refusal cites the rule or precondition. Costs one of sixty messages an hour (a failed one a quarter).

tools.name: observe
tools.description: See the world as yourself through an observation query: a root (self, here, window, palace, {"room": key}, {"entity": id}), components and fields to select, relations to follow (contents, in, exits), where filters, limit; "timed": "curve" returns timed fields as curves. You see exactly the fields yo

findings.title: Toxic flow: untrusted input can reach an external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: check · Public sink: gate · Destructive: check.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: check · Public sink: gate · Destructive: check

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
